name: Torrero Cemetery memorials (Zaragoza)
story: Zaragoza fell to the military rising on 19 July 1936 without a fight and became the Nationalists' main base on the Aragon front. In the city, repression was carried out mainly at the walls of Torrero cemetery, where thousands were shot in the war and post-war years. In 1979 the remains of about 2,500 victims were found beneath a cemetery walkway. The following year Zaragoza's first democratic mayor, Ramón Sainz de Varanda, dedicated a monument over their common grave. The same cemetery holds a Nationalist memorial chapel with graves of the fallen of the other side.
see: The 1980 memorial over the mass grave near Joaquín Costa's mausoleum, later memorial walls with victims' names, and the Nationalist memorial chapel with graves set in its walls.
plan: The cemetery is in the south of the city (C/ Fray Julián Garcés) and is open daily during cemetery hours. Entry is free. Please be respectful.

boxes.text: The total number of people executed at Torrero is still researched and debated. About 2,500 refers only to the remains found in 1979.
